From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Package Review (Buyer Side)

## Preliminary point: the "reviewer efficiency note" should not be followed

The Seller's package says [STANDARD] clauses have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and need no scrutiny. Nothing in the file shows that. Our playbook does not accept these positions, and most of the [STANDARD] items are direct departures from it. I have reviewed the whole package, not only the [OPEN] items. The note also dates from the Seller's side and is not an instruction to us.

The disclosure letter is also as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. Any bring-down needs to cover that gap.

## 1. Limitation package (Clauses 12.1, 12.2, 12.3/13)

| Issue | Seller draft | Playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m starting position | Reject. 20% is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given. |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Restore AUD 5,000. |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject. Restore AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery. |
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months | Reject. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. |
| Universal limitation | Any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Reject. This would import the general limits into Title, Tax, IP and covenant claims. |

**Reasoning:** Together these items cut recoverable general claims substantially. A AUD 250,000 basket with excess-only recovery means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250,000 of general losses. The universal limitation clause would then override the separate regimes we require.

## 2. Fundamental / Title claims

- **Seller draft:** capacity and title warranties subject to the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Pushback:** reject outright. Title and capacity are core to what the Buyer is paying for, and the Seller's own disclosure (DL §10) relies only on a share register.

## 3. Fraud and exclusive remedies (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

- **Seller draft:** limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Pushback:** insert the fraud carve-out. Without it, the Seller could rely on the limits to shield deliberate misstatements, including in the disclosure letter.

## 4. Disclosure (Schedule 7; DL §1.1 and §1.2)

- **Seller draft:** general disclosure of the whole data room (including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Pushback:** delete the general disclosure. Disclosure must be specific and fairly describe the matter. Also note that DL §1.1 is tied to a data room snapshot at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, and any later changes would be captured by general disclosure without an express update.

## 5. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3)

- **Seller draft:** no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and can never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Pushback:** delete. This clause would effectively turn every disclosed issue (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, the incident) into a Buyer-risk item, which conflicts with the specific protections we need.

## 6. Specific completion items

**Bluefen (Clauses 3/6.3; DL §2)**
- **Seller draft:** reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Playbook:** effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Facts:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (~30%). The DL confirms no final consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions.
- **Pushback:** make effective consent plus evidence of satisfied conditions a condition precedent to Completion. Delete the deemed-satisfaction language.

**Riverlark (Clauses 2/7; DL §3)**
- **Seller draft:** release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Playbook:** current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. A post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Facts:** about AUD 3.2m outstanding, not repaid, no discharge in the data room.
- **Pushback:** require payout at Completion from the funds flow, with releases delivered at Completion. Any post-Completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's written approval.

**Employee bonuses (DD-005; DL §5; funds flow)**
- **Seller draft:** AUD 420,000 bonuses excluded from the funds flow, described as "a matter for the Seller."
- **Playbook:** a specific line item or Seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Gap:** on-costs (payroll tax, super) are not quantified and may be triggered by Completion.
- **Pushback:** add a specific funds flow line for the AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs, or require Seller funding. Obtain an on-cost calculation.

**Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1; DD-004 cl 7.3; DD-010; DL §4)**
- **Seller draft:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate."
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure.
- **Facts:** SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. This is not bank verification either way, and we should not treat it as a confirmed debt or as settled.
- **Pushback:** broaden the indemnity to cover IP title and transfer, keep the SOW3 cure, and require bank or payment evidence to verify the AUD 180,000 position.

**Export/privacy incident (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6; DD-006; DL §6)**
- **Seller draft:** "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material."
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate and require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Facts:** a download link went to an unintended external address; about 1,240 records may be involved; access, scope and notification are all unknown.
- **Pushback:** reject the "not material" characterisation as unsupported. Require log preservation, a completed investigation with updates before Completion, and specific protection for the matter. Do not assign a loss figure or assume a breach. The specific protection is a negotiating point that goes slightly beyond the playbook and should be confirmed with Amelia Frost.

**Sandbar renewals (DD-008, DD-011; DL §8; AUD 330,000)**
- **Seller draft:** ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Playbook:** assess them. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Pushback:** require the contracts, termination rights and accrual position for each renewal. Check whether DD-008 and DD-011 describe the same three renewals, to avoid double-counting. Do not accept or reject the classification until the assessment is done.

## 7. Tax and IP (Seller summary)

- **Seller draft:** tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime."
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain open, with no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Pushback:** reject. These are not settled, and they must sit in their own categories rather than the general regime. Tax and IP should be marked open in the mark-up.

## 8. Title evidence (DD-012; DL §10)

- **Seller draft:** title evidenced by the Company share register.
- **Playbook:** DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof. Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority.
- **Pushback:** require ASIC company and share register searches, PPSR searches and any other independent registry evidence before Completion.

## 9. Items outside the playbook (for deal team confirmation)

These are not covered by the playbook, so please confirm the approach before raising them:
- **Office lease (DL §7):** the notification obligation may or may not require landlord consent for the share sale. Ask the Seller to confirm, and check whether consent is needed for Completion.
- **Mossvale (DL §9):** the assignment restriction may or may not apply to a share sale. Ask the Seller to confirm whether Mossvale consent is required.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "cleared" framing.** Review all clauses, and do not treat the [STANDARD] items as agreed.
2. **Restore the limitation package:** 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket, 24-month general period. Do not offer 20% or 18 months without Amelia Frost's written authority for the draft.
3. **Separate the regimes:** Title and capacity at 100% cap, six years, outside the general limits. Delete the universal limitation clause. Keep Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate.
4. **Insert the fraud carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
5. **Replace the disclosure framework** with specific fair disclosure only. Delete the data room, public register and general Accounts disclosure.
6. **Delete the buyer-knowledge exclusion** (Clause 8.3).
7. **Bluefen:** effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions before Completion.
8. **Riverlark:** payout from Completion funds and releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific funds flow line or Seller-funded.
10. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, keep the SOW3 cure, and verify the AUD 180,000 with bank evidence.
11. **Incident:** log preservation, investigation with updates, and specific protection, with no assumed breach or numeric demand.
12. **Sandbar:** assess the renewals without automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
13. **Title:** independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is not sufficient.
14. **Tax and IP:** mark as open. Not settled, not capped under the general regime.
15. **Bring-down:** update all disclosures from 22 September 2026 to the current date and Completion.
